vulnerable_statements.reason: The parent HWPT is validated only for auto_domain/nest_parent; it never checks that parent->common.domain->owner matches the ops of the device's IOMMU driver. On a system with several IOMMU drivers, userspace can pass a nest-parent HWPT created by one driver together with a device behind another driver.

The foreign parent domain goes to this driver's domain_alloc_user. The driver then casts it to its own domain type (for example with container_of/to_xxx_domain) and reads or writes fields that do not exist. This is type confusion and can corrupt memory or read out of bounds.

suggested_fix: Before allocating the nested domain, check that the parent domain belongs to the same IOMMU driver. For example, extend the check to `if (parent->auto_domain || !parent->nest_parent || parent->common.domain->owner != ops) return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);`. Then domain_alloc_user only ever gets a parent domain of its own type.
